## Summary

**279_R6FIX.16** — BL-116 (handoff RH-A1-5, verified at `277_R6LOW.1`): the signed
one-click email action consumed on GET at both mounts (`/api/action/:token` and
`/action/:token`). A mail gateway's link-scanner prefetch burned the single-use
token (the recipient's real click then lands on the 410 page), and the `hold` arm
called `holdGate` on GET — a scanner pause of the gate countdown ("Wait for me")
with no user intent.

This is the RH-31 defect class `275_R6WEB.1` fixed for magic links; the BL row asks
for the shared pattern, so this applies it on the api:

- **GET** on both mounts renders a no-consume confirm page — a `<form method="post">`
  back to the same URL with `data-email-action-confirm` on the submit (mirroring
  `data-magic-link-confirm`). No verify, no consume, no `holdGate`, no DB read.
- **POST** on both mounts runs `consumeSignedAction` unchanged: HMAC verify + the
  atomic single-use consume + `holdGate` for `hold` + 303 to the §4.2 deep link.
  The 400/410 page contract moves verbatim from the GET arm.

Tests: consume assertions moved to POST on the four existing arms; the minted-URL
contract (DEF.3 / STB.3 F9 — the emailed URL must answer) now asserts GET 200 →
POST 303 → replay POST 410; a new pin runs two GET prefetches across both mounts
and proves the gate untouched and the token still live for the real confirm.

No emissions changed, no check weakened, single-use/expiry/HMAC guarantees
untouched (the conditional UPDATE stays the only consume path).
